more_info.overview: Iron oxides and iron hydroxides is used as a color in food. Its technological role is to add or restore food colour.
more_info.uses: EU permissions include entire fresh fruit and vegetables, fruit and vegetable preparations excluding compote, processed fish and fishery products including molluscs and crustaceans. These permissions depend on the food category and its conditions of use.
more_info.origin: Iron oxides and hydroxides are manufactured synthetically and purified to limit contamination by other metals. The different oxide forms provide yellow, red, brown or black pigments.
more_info.side_effects:
EFSA could not complete a food-additive safety assessment in 2015 because the available data were insufficient.
Some laboratory cell tests were positive for DNA effects; their significance for human food exposure remained unresolved.
